what_happened: The person running Athena wrote three requests today that named an earlier job, or its design file, as background. In each case the earlier job had been rejected and its design note never landed. The reader treated that note as present in the snapshot. It built the reading on the missing file, and the reading was refused. This happened twice for the pass-over fix and twice for the merge-wait fix. The requests were re-queued without the references. This is an intervention note, not a failed job record.
cause: Nothing resolves a job id or file path cited in a request against the current snapshot or the job's landed state before the reader uses it. A rejected job's outputs look the same as a landed job's outputs in a request's text. The request writer is not told that citing a job as background makes the reader rely on its deliverables. The reader treats every named job as present. The gap shows only when the reading is refused, and the same pattern was repeated across several requests in one day.
prevention: Add a check at reading acceptance. For each job id or design-file path in the request, look up the job's final state and confirm the cited file exists in the snapshot. If the job was rejected or never landed, or the file is missing, flag the reference as not present, and require the reading to take no dependency on it. Show the writer a warning at queue time. The check would also cover the already-known reader case, where a reading assumes a prior job's deliverable exists.
proposed_request: When a request is queued or read, check each job id and each file path it names. For a job id, look up its final state (landed, rejected, abandoned). For a path, check that it exists in the current snapshot. If a cited job did not land, or a cited file is absent, print a warning at queue time naming the reference. Also give the reader a list of references that are not present, with an instruction to build nothing on them and to state the needed facts from the request itself. Acceptance: (1) a request citing a rejected job's design file produces the warning and a reading that does not rely on the file; (2) a request citing a landed job and an existing file produces no warning; (3) a test covers both cases using real record shapes. Apply this check to evidence-only citations as well as dependencies.
